name: Republic of Chile

areaKm2.note: asOf 2024. Surface area 756,556 km2 (AG.SRF.TOTL.K2); low is land area 742,032 km2 (AG.LND.TOTL.K2). Excludes the Antarctic claim; includes Easter Island and Juan Fernandez.

population.note: asOf 2025 (World Bank SP.POP.TOTL 19,859,921). Low/high +/-1% for 2026 change and census revision. Everything inside ne:CHL.

activePersonnel.note: IISS Military Balance 2025 p.404 as quoted: 68,500 active (excludes 44,700 Carabineros). CIA Factbook 2025: ~70,000 (40,000 Army, 20,000 Navy, 10,000 Air Force).

trainedReserves.note: IISS Military Balance 2025: 19,100 reserves. High is an educated allowance for recent conscript classes.

supportPersonnel.note: Active 68,500 (IISS 2025) minus infantry P roles (6,000 + 12,000). Covers navy and air force, armour/artillery crews, logistics and staff.

mobilizationRatio.note: Analogy to conscription-backed small-to-middle powers; Chile keeps selective conscription and stored Leopard/Marder fleets. Educated judgement.

count.note: Educated guess. Mechanized infantry of the northern armoured brigades on Marder 1A3 and M113/YPR-765. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_equipment_of_the_Chilean_Army)

training.note: Rubric 0.75: professional cadre with selective conscription; NATO-standard equipment and exercises (UNITAS, RIMPAC, Red Flag).

count.note: Educated guess. Mountain, motorized, airborne/special-forces infantry and ~3,500 marines. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_equipment_of_the_Chilean_Army)

training.note: Rubric 0.75: professional cadre with selective conscription; NATO-standard equipment and exercises (UNITAS, RIMPAC, Red Flag).

count.note: Equipment list: Leopard 2A4CHL ~186 purchased (some for spares/storage); Leopard 1V (<200 purchased 1997) largely replaced and stored. Low ~130 reflects IISS-style active counts.

quality.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: Leopard 2A4, rated by IISS as the only modern MBT fleet in South America.

quality.note: Rubric 0.5: Marder and AIFV are 1970s-80s designs.

count.note: Chilean Air Force inventory: F-16C/D Block 50 10 + F-16AM/BM MLU 36 + F-5E/F Tiger III 8+3 = 57. Low allows for F-5 retirement.

quality.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: F-16 Block 50 with AIM-120, MLU fleet; E-3D AEW support.

training.note: Rubric 0.75: Red Flag participation, NATO-standard flying hours.

count.note: Air Force: UH-1H 13 + Bell 206 5 + S-70/UH-60 7 + Bell 412 16 = 41; Army: AS532 Cougar 8 + SA330 Puma 2 + MD530F 9 = 19 (Army equipment list); Navy ~15 (AS532SC, Bell 412, Dauphin; educated). Total ~75.
Hermes 900 3 + Mantis 2 = 5 Air Force; Navy ScanEagle (educated). Army Lascar/SpyLite minis excluded.
Active ships list: Type 22 (Almirante Williams) 1 + Type 23 3 + Adelaide class 2 + Karel Doorman class 2 = 8 frigates. Low allows for retirement of the oldest Type 22.

quality.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: ex-European/Australian frigates with SM-2/ESSM/Harpoon, upgraded.

count.note: Active ships list: OPV-80 4 + Taitao 4 + Sa'ar 4 FAC 3 + LPD Sargento Aldea 1 + BATRAL LST 2 + Elicura 1 = 15 (low); mid/high add Protector-class 16 and Ona/Alacalufe 3 coastal patrol craft.

Army equipment list: Mistral 1 on Unimog with EL/M-2106 radars (quantity not given); Air Force ground air-defence units not itemised on the fetched pages. ~12 short-range batteries is an educated conversion.

commandQuality.note: Rubric 0.75: Prussian-tradition professional staff system, NATO interoperability; no war since 1883 apart from 1978 Beagle crisis mobilization.

cohesion.note: Rubric 0.75: professional with strong unit identity.

morale.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: high for northern/Andean defence; post-2019 domestic deployment fatigue.

weapons.note: Anchor 9: Spike LR/ER, AIM-120, Harpoon, SM-2; no long-range land fires.

armor.note: Anchor 9: Leopard 2A4 composite armour; no active protection.

fortification.note: Anchor 8-9: northern defensive positions; limited air defence.

logistics.note: Anchor 9: KC-135 tankers, C-130, ASMAR shipyards; long narrow territory with single trunk highway.

communications.note: Anchor 9: Link 16 on F-16, NATO-compatible C2.

isr.note: Anchor 9: E-3D Sentry AEW (2), FASAT-Delta satellite, Hermes 900.

gdpPerCapita.note: asOf 2025. Rebased GDP 490,662,575,745 / population 19,859,921 = 24,706 2011 int$. Range +/-10%. Corrected 2026-10-29: values x1.0376 because the rebase factor was an arithmetic error (0.8005); the right factor is 0.8306 (FRED GDPDEF, 2017=100: 2011 91.478 / 2021 110.130). Figures quoted above are before the correction.

gdp.note: asOf 2025. World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.PP.KD (constant 2021 int$) 612,945,128,976 x 0.8005 (US GDP deflator 2011/2021) = 490,662,575,745 2011 int$. Range +/-10% for PPP benchmark uncertainty and the relative-price drift the rebase ignores. Series: https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/CHL/indicator/NY.GDP.MKTP.PP.KD?format=json Corrected 2026-10-29: values x1.0376 because the rebase factor was an arithmetic error (0.8005); the right factor is 0.8306 (FRED GDPDEF, 2017=100: 2011 91.478 / 2021 110.130). Figures quoted above are before the correction.

milSpendShare.note: SIPRI via World Bank: 1.52% of GDP in 2025. CIA Factbook 1.5% (2023-24), 2.0% (2020-21). Copper Law earmarking replaced in 2019 by a strategic contingency fund.

industrialShare.note: asOf 2025: industry incl. construction 31.42% of GDP (NV.IND.TOTL.ZS). Mining (copper, lithium) is the largest component.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess. Large exporter of fruit, wine, salmon; imports cereals; not computed from FAO balance sheets.

annualCohort.note: asOf 2025. Males reaching military age per year = male population 9,871,188 (SP.POP.TOTL.MA.IN) x share of males aged 15-19 6.318% (SP.POP.1519.MA.5Y) / 5 = 124,726. Males only (conscript-pool convention); about double if women are counted. Range +/-10%.

ships_minor.note: Educated guess. ASMAR Talcahuano builds OPV-80s and the Escotillon IV multipurpose ships. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_active_Chilean_Navy_ships)

ifv_apc.note: Educated guess. FAMAE assembles/upgrades Piranha and other vehicles in small numbers. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_equipment_of_the_Chilean_Army)

roadKm.note: CIA World Factbook as quoted: 85,983 km total (2020), 21,289 km paved, 64,695 unpaved, 3,347 km controlled-access. Mid is paved plus half the unpaved network (derived midpoint); high is the total.

railKm.note: World Bank 2,396 km (2021, state EFE network) as low; CIA Factbook 7,281 km (2014) incl. private mining lines as high; mid an educated middle.

majorPorts.note: CIA Factbook 2024: 39 ports, 0 large + 2 medium + 10 small; 12 key ports named (Valparaiso, San Antonio, Talcahuano, Antofagasta, Iquique, Arica, Punta Arenas...). Mid counts the main container/naval ports.

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess. Chile is below the 1 million GT threshold of the merchant-fleet table (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_merchant_navy_capacity_by_country); CIA Factbook 2023 counts 249 merchant ships (66 general cargo, 14 tankers).

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Truck and coastal-shipping sustainment along a 4,300 km north-south axis.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Horses and mules; not from FAO data. Mountain units use mules.

nuclearWarheads.note: Chile is a non-nuclear-weapon state (NPT); not listed by FAS Status of World Nuclear Forces. Party to Tlatelolco.

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.2: Andes wall and Atacama desert, fortified northern frontier, population support; high 1.3 for the desert/Andean climate.

notes: Modern snapshot, asOf 2025 data with 2026 order of battle. Population convention: everything inside ne:CHL (World Bank). Money in 2011 int$ via derived:ppp-rebase-2011. Force counts: IISS Military Balance 2025 (personnel) as quoted; Chilean Army equipment list, Chilean Air Force inventory and the active Chilean Navy ships list. ships_major = frigates; ships_minor = OPVs, patrol, FAC, LPD/LST; drones = Group 2+ UAVs. Infantry P-role splits are educated guesses (grade D). Carabineros (44,700) excluded.
